description: Gritting Routes - Scotland is a dataset listed in UK national open data portal, an open data portal, published or maintained by Scottish Government SpatialData.gov.scot. Each local authority creates gritting routes and regimes to keep their most important roads (and in some cases footpaths) and networks clear come bad winter weather. Most LAs create these as line datasets. So the national dataset is a line format dataset. We now have two layers: one for road gritting and one for footpath. Coverage: Scottish Government SpatialData.gov.scot. The portal files it under the publisher Scottish Government SpatialData.gov.scot. Its tags are Transport networks, Utility and governmental services. The portal shows 2026-08-04 as the last metadata change. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the portal listing (dataset page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support traffic, parking and road network studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-ckan-uk-portal.
